title: Sandridge Road / Lake Asbury / First Coast Expressway land & development activity
description: District 5's Lake Asbury area is undergoing rapid change: the county-funded Sandridge Road (CR 739B) widening ($31.6M, per the county's own project page), a 2005 Lake Asbury Master Plan, a 2021 moratorium on new rezoning within the master-plan area, growth pressure tied to the First Coast Expressway, and a 2025 inter-neighborhood "connectivity" rezoning-adjacent plan that was withdrawn after public opposition. The lead is whether specific land sales, rezonings, or comprehensive-plan amendments in this corridor show a pattern connecting county infrastructure spending, private landowners/developers, and BCC/District 5 decisions.
origin: User-provided investigative lead (mission brief), refined against initial search research 2026-09-11.
entitiesInvolved: Clay County Public Works / Bonded Transportation Program
whyItMatters: Road-widening and rezoning decisions directly affect adjacent land values; if any BCC vote or land-use approval in this corridor coincided with a documented financial or personal relationship, that intersection would be a Voting-Conflict/Ethics lead, not by itself an allegation.
evidenceAvailable: Official county project page for the Sandridge Road widening (source: county Bonded Transportation Program). News coverage of the 2025 connectivity-plan withdrawal and general Lake Asbury growth pressure (secondary).
evidenceMissing: No parcel-level ownership chain (property appraiser → seller → buyer → LLC) has been built. No specific rezoning/comprehensive-plan-amendment case tied to this corridor has been pulled from BCC agendas/minutes. No confirmation of Burke's specific votes on any Lake Asbury/Sandridge-corridor item.

This is currently the only confirmed Gustafson-related BCC matter found. Whether there is a broader Gustafson family/company footprint in Clay County land or development records, and whether it connects to Burke or District 5 beyond this one case, is unresolved.

title: Stormwater assessment decision-making and Burke's role as Board Chair
description: Clay County adopted a new stormwater assessment fee (based on impervious surface area, roughly $51-$161/year for a single-family home) alongside hardship and disabled-veteran exemptions. News coverage describes Board Chair Kristen Burke chairing a contentious public hearing, described as frustrated with attendees and threatening to eject people for clapping or speaking out of turn. ClayMoneyTrail's existing money-trail dataset already carries the official stormwater revenue/cost estimates (sourceId: stormwater-impact) — this lead is about the decision-making process and Burke's specific role, not the dollar figures, which are handled in the main money-trail dataset.

evidenceAvailable: Multiple secondary news accounts (Action News Jax, WOKV) of hearings, exemption votes, and Burke's conduct as chair. Official county business-impact estimate already in ClayMoneyTrail's money dataset.

title: Commissioner compensation increase proposal

The Charter Review Commission — a separate advisory body from the BCC itself — has reportedly discussed raising it, with different secondary sources citing figures from roughly $60,000 up to 'triple' the current salary, and reporting Charter Review Chair Courtney Connor opposed. Whether Burke has personally advocated for or against any specific figure has not been established.
